title: Regional Fallback Economics & Supply Simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build an evidence-backed simulator and decision guide that quantifies the customer cost, latency, and quality impact of regional model outages or supplier constraints and recommends procurement/tradeoff thresholds for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Why: product and GTM need a defensible, quantitative way to recommend fallback policies (model substitution, region failover, reserved capacity triggers) to customers and sales, and to inform procurement commit sizes. Current signals are fragmented across latency dashboards, model supply watchlists, and one-off field notes.

Scope: produce a lightweight Monte Carlo simulator + deterministic scenarios covering: regional capacity loss (short/medium/long), quantization/variant substitution quality delta, cross-region egress latency cost, reserved capacity stepping thresholds, and customer-sensitive SLO violation cost. Deliverables: 1) Simulation workbook (BigQuery + Colab), 2) Decision thresholds doc for Sales/SEs, 3) 2 pilot customer analyses, 4) integration spec for Console to surface recommended fallback props.

Key questions: Which supply events create >10% uplift in expected per-request cost? When does reserved capacity (Dedicated) become cheaper than multi-region fallbacks? How much quality degradation is tolerable for different buyer archetypes before recommending private on-prem options?

Data sources: latency histograms (Console/Prometheus), token cost ledger (Billing), model-variant quality deltas (research/evals), regional capacity telemetry (infra), public provider outage history (vendor signals).

Methodology: combine Monte Carlo sampling of traffic patterns + scenario sweeps for deterministic triggers. Sensitivity analysis on traffic skew, quantization-induced latency savings, and failover frequency. Use customer archetypes (latency-first, cost-first, compliance-first) to parametrize value of quality/latency tradeoffs.

Stakeholders: PM (owner), Research (quality deltas), Eng infra (capacity telemetry), Solutions (pilot customers), Sales Ops (procurement thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator accepts region-level capacity, model-variant latency/quality, and traffic profile inputs
Simulator outputs per-request expected cost, 95th latency, and quality-probability curves for each fallback policy
Decision guide with clear procurement thresholds (e.g., reserved GPU sizing heuristics) is approved by Sales Ops
Two pilot customer analyses completed with documented recommendations and customer feedback
tech_risks: Quality deltas between model variants are noisy and dataset-dependent — mitigated by using multiple eval suites
Telemetry gaps in historical regional capacity events — mitigated by synthetic stress tests and vendor incident proxies
Modeling assumptions may misrepresent tail-latency under massive failovers — include conservative tail multipliers and validation in pilot
